newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-FIORENTINA LOOK TO BATISTUTA TO REGAIN FORM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIORENTINA LOOK TO BATISTUTA TO REGAIN FORM.

text.p: Italy's Fiorentina will be hoping star Argentine striker Gabriel Batistuta rediscovers the route to goal for Thursday's European Cup Winners' Cup quarter-final clash with Benfica.
With both teams struggling in their domestic leagues, success in Europe offers the chance of salvaging some glory from a disappointing season.
Fiorentina, with the usually prolific Batistuta suddenly finding scoring difficult, are languishing 12th in the Italian league only five points clear of the relegation zone.
Benfica are third in Portugal but 14 points adrift of title-holders and leaders Porto.
"It is a challenge that is going to stimulate both sides. We are going to do everything possible to make the next round," said Benfica coach Manuel Jose.
Both teams have injury problems and their difficulties are compounded by the fact that several key players cannot be used because they have already played for other teams in Europe this season.

Brazilian midfielder Alexandre Amaral, formerly of Italy's Parma, and Dutch winger Glen Helder, formerly with English club Arsenal, will both be watching from the stands where they could be joined by Benfica's playmaker Valdo Filho who has injured his right leg.
Fiorentina will be without Russian winger Andrei Kanchelskis, formerly of Everton, and injured midfielder Massimo Orlando.
But the Italians will be happy enough if Batistuta, their inspirational captain, can refind his touch in the first leg clash.

The Argentine has been criticised for some seemingly poor performances recently, but coach Claudio Ranieri believes he will prove his worth against Benfica, twice winners in the European Cup but who are looking for their first Cup Winners' title.
"Gabriel (Batistuta) is not the sort of player who gets depressed...I think you'll find that he has a great wish to prove to everybody that he is still the Batistuta," he said.
Benfica - Michel Preud'Homme, Pedro Henriques, Jorge Soares, Jorge Bermudez, El Hadrioui, Jose Calado, Jamir Gomes, Tahar Kalej, Edgar Pacheco, Joao Pinto, Nica Panduru.

Fiorentina - Francesco Toldo, Daniele Carnesciali, Pasquale Padalino, Giulio Falcone, Michele Serena, Giovanni Piacentini, Stefan Schwarz, Emiliano Bigica, Rui Costa, Gabriel Batistuta, Francesco Baiano.
